grammar.title: Future Forms: Going To, Will and Present Continuous
grammar.explanation:
We use **going to** for plans we already made. She **is going to** take an exam tomorrow, so she feels a little worried.

We use **will** for quick decisions we make now. The phone rings, and I **will** answer it.

We also use **will** for promises. Do not be lonely. I **will** call you tonight, I promise.

We use the **present continuous** (am/is/are + verb-ing) for fixed plans with a time. We **are meeting** our friends at six o'clock.

Be careful: **going to** is for plans, **will** is for quick decisions and promises. Do not say I **will to** call you. Say I **will** call you.
examples: I *am going to* cook dinner for my family tonight. (plan)
She *is going to* study hard because she feels nervous about the test. (plan)
The phone is ringing. I *will* answer it. (quick decision)
You will not be lonely. I *will* visit you on Sunday, I promise. (promise)
We *are meeting* our friends at six o'clock. (fixed plan)
He *is starting* his new job on Monday. He is grateful for the chance. (fixed plan)
